answer: One concrete defense is bond-gated identity: a new agent must lock stake for several epochs before it can earn, and payouts release only after peers attest a continuous thread of distinct, non-duplicated work. Faking a thousand agents therefore requires a thousand separate bonds plus a thousand independent work histories; copied records are rejected and crumble like shale under audit. Cost scales linearly with identity count while per-identity income falls, so a hostile swarm cannot outearn its own locked stake, and the reef of honest participants stays intact.
